creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA asks whether MercadoLibre's crash is a buying opportunity after management spooked investors with an aggressive spending push: a lower free-delivery threshold to boost engagement and an expanded logistics footprint of warehouses to cut cost per customer at scale. Early signs support the strategy: results on 4 November showed net revenue up 41% year over year, monthly active users up 29%, financial-services assets under management up 67%, and cost per shipment in Brazil down 5% despite high inflation. Analysts have trimmed long-term EPS growth estimates from about 34% in January to about 28%, still an excellent rate, he says, and he backs management's approach given its record: operating margin was 25% in 2017, fell to minus 10% in an earlier investment cycle, recovered to about 15%, and is now 8.26% and falling again as spending rises. He sees the same invest-then-grow pattern repeating. The stock trades at a forward P/E of 27, its cheapest in years and below its EPS growth estimate. His discounted cash flow model, with lower near-term free cash flow, higher free cash flow from 2029, and a higher risk premium and risk-free rate after Brazil's election, gives a fair value of $2,213 against a current price of $1,512. Call: MELI BUY — risks are higher, but he judges the upside worth taking for a long-term investor.
title: Why Is MELI Stock Crashing, and is it a Buying Opportunity?

calls.thesis: BUY (was BUY 17 Oct) — aggressive investment push (lower free-delivery threshold, logistics expansion) is spooking investors, but Q4 showed revenue +41%, monthly active users +29%, fintech AUM +67%, and Brazil cost per shipment down 5% despite inflation. He backs the spend: management has invested and recovered margins before (25% in 2017, down to -10%, back to ~15%). Risks higher, upside worth it.
calls.base_case: Near-30% EPS growth (revised down from ~34%) with investment paying off from 2029; FV $2,213.
calls.bull_case: Investments compound into the Latin America e-commerce/fintech tailwind; margins recover toward prior cycle highs.
calls.bear_case: Brazil election outcome and higher regional rates/volatility keep margins compressed; Wall Street keeps cutting EPS estimates.
